subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: Should browser routes intentionally return the stale acted-on target and require explicit re-selection whenever a backend cannot prove target continuity, instead of retaining current heuristic continuation?
rationale: This is an intentional compatibility and recovery-policy change affecting existing browser automation clients; source review can establish the tradeoff but cannot choose the permanent user contract.

options.title: Accept fail-safe continuity
options.body: Merge after a rebase if the browser owner accepts stale-target re-selection as the supported response when backend continuity is unavailable.

options.title: Keep heuristic continuation
options.body: Do not merge this route-contract change and retain or redesign a compatibility-preserving recovery path with an explicit identity guarantee.

options.title: Split backend contracts further
options.body: Land only backend paths with an approved identity owner and track any remaining backend-specific continuity design separately.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-safe continuity
recommendation.body: Merge after a rebase if the browser owner accepts stale-target re-selection as the supported response when backend continuity is unavailable.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report and PR discussion identify this person as the browser-contract decision owner.
